table.title: Civil and Criminal Cases Decided by the Supreme Court 1945 to 1948 (Jan.-June)
footnotes: Remarks: The figures do not include cases handled by the two branch courts of the Supreme Court.
transcriber_notes: Rows: 12 months as printed, plus Grand Total. Table printed sideways on p. 208; read from a rotated crop.
'..' printed for July–December 1948 (no data), kept as printed.

Column totals: 1945 — Civil: printed 8,896, the 12 months sum to 8,996 — does NOT reconcile (diff 100); re-read, kept as printed. The Grand Total row is also internally inconsistent: 8,896 + 2,921 = 11,817, not the printed 11,917 (which does equal the sum of the 1945 Total column). The text on p. 205 gives 40,182 civil cases 1945–June 1948, which matches the month sums (8,996) rather than the printed 8,896. All other 11 Grand Total figures reconcile.
Row totals: Civil + Criminal = Total in every row.
Printed 'January:' with a colon (misprint for dot leader), kept as 'January'.

table.title: Civil and Criminal Cases Involving Foreigners 1945 to 1947 First Trial (By Locality)
transcriber_notes: Rows: 19 provinces/municipalities as printed, plus Grand Total. Table printed sideways on p. 212; read from a rotated crop.

Figures are printed out of line with the labels: every figure column sits roughly half a line (1945–46) to a full line (1947) below its row label, so e.g. the 1947 figures 587/235/822 sit level with 'Kiangsu'. Each column has exactly 19 figure lines (including '..') for 19 labels, so they were assigned in order (first line = Nanking); on that reading the large figures fall to Shanghai, consistent with the text ('Most of these were tried in Shanghai').
'..' printed for nil entries, kept as printed.
Column totals: all 9 Grand Total figures reconcile with the sums of the rows. Row totals: Civil + Criminal = Total in every row and year.
Grand totals 126 (1945), 959 (1946), 962 (1947) match the text on p. 211.

transcriber_notes: Rows: 37 as printed, plus Grand Total.

'Hsingan' as printed (spelled 'Hingan' in Table 1).

The few non-nil figures in the Branch, Juvenile and Colony columns sit between rows in places (e.g. Juvenile '1' between Jehol and Chahar, between Kiangsi and Hupeh); assigned to the row whose printed Total they make add up — the printed Total was used only to place a clearly-read figure, not to read a digit.

Column totals: Prison printed 121, parts sum to 121 — reconciles; Branch Prison printed 12, parts sum to 12 — reconciles; Juvenile Prison printed 4, parts sum to 4 — reconciles; Convicts' Colony printed 2, parts sum to 2 — reconciles; Detention House printed 1,878, parts sum to 1,878 — reconciles; Total printed 2,017, parts sum to 2,017 — reconciles

Text p. 216 gives 121 prisons, 12 branch prisons, four juvenile prisons, two convicts' colonies, 1,878 detention houses — matches the printed totals.
